clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: Which pair of situations requires hand hygiene before the nursing task according to current CDC guidance?

options.A: Before touching a client and before performing an aseptic task.
options.B: Before reading the client's chart and before entering the medication room.
options.C: Before answering the unit telephone and before documenting vital signs.
options.D: Before speaking with a visitor and before leaving the nurses' station.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC healthcare hand-hygiene guidance lists immediately before touching a patient and before performing an aseptic task as clinical indications for hand hygiene. CDC also identifies additional indications such as after touching a patient or the patient's surroundings, after contact with blood or body fluids, after glove removal, and before moving from a soiled to a clean body site on the same patient. Options B, C, and D describe routine unit activities that are not themselves listed as the two pre-care hand-hygiene indications tested here.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Perform hand hygiene immediately before touching a client and before an aseptic task as two CDC-defined pre-care indications.

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends hand hygiene immediately before touching a patient and before performing an aseptic task such as placing or handling an invasive device.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: replaced the WHO-specific framing with current CDC hand-hygiene guidance per source hierarchy; removed absolute distractors and rebuilt all choices as parallel two-situation pairs with an exact NCSBN infection-prevention locator.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was correct but relied on WHO despite adequate current CDC guidance and used three obvious 'only' distractors. The revised item uses the preferred U.S. infection-control authority and parallel paired situations.

option_audit.A: Correct. Both situations are explicit CDC indications for hand hygiene before care.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. These activities are not the CDC pre-care clinical indications tested in the stem.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Telephone use and documentation are not the two CDC pre-care indications listed in A.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. These routine communication/location activities do not replace the CDC indications before patient contact or aseptic care.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone contains two explicit CDC pre-care hand-hygiene indications.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel pairs of pre-task situations of comparable length; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
